questions.title: Access Token vs Refresh Token
questions.question: What is the difference between an access token and a refresh token?
searchIntent: difference between access token and refresh token
questions.realWorldScenario: Standard JWT auth implementation with short-lived access tokens and long-lived refresh tokens.

questions.title: Why Access Tokens Are Short-Lived
questions.question: Why are access tokens typically set to expire in 15 minutes rather than 24 hours?
searchIntent: why are access tokens short lived
questions.realWorldScenario: Minimising the damage window if an access token is stolen.

questions.title: Silent Refresh Flow
questions.question: What is a silent refresh and how does it allow users to stay logged in without being interrupted?
searchIntent: how to auto refresh JWT token React
questions.realWorldScenario: User is filling in a long form — token expires before they submit; silent refresh prevents forced logout.

questions.title: Refresh Token Rotation
questions.question: What is refresh token rotation and why is it a security best practice?
questions.realWorldScenario: Detecting stolen refresh tokens — if an old refresh token is used, the family is revoked.

questions.title: Handling 401 on Token Expiry
questions.question: How does a React frontend detect that an access token has expired and obtain a new one automatically?
searchIntent: how to handle expired JWT React
questions.realWorldScenario: User gets a 401 while browsing — the app should silently refresh and retry, not show a login screen.

questions.title: Where to Store the Refresh Token
questions.question: Where should you store a refresh token on the client, and why?
searchIntent: where to store refresh token securely
questions.realWorldScenario: Refresh tokens are long-lived so their storage security is even more critical than access tokens.

questions.title: The exp Claim in JWT
questions.question: What is the exp claim in a JWT and how does the server use it to validate the token?
questions.realWorldScenario: Server checks the exp claim on every request to reject expired tokens without any database lookup.
